info.title: openHC IO over MQTT
info.description:
The live state and control surface of an openHC controller: IO (relays, contacts, IR, serial, front-panel LEDs — iod), audio (ohc-audiod), health (sysmond) and return-to-stock (iod), all on the controller's own mosquitto.

The rule: anything a control system (Home Assistant, Control4) acts on or watches change is here; configuration and things that rarely change are REST (see the OpenAPI document) — the audio endpoint map, the MQTT settings, full-resolution telemetry history.

**Three prefixes.** `state/` is RETAINED, so a subscriber that connects an hour late is told the truth immediately. `event/` is NOT retained, because 'a remote was pressed' must never be replayed to whoever connects next. `cmd/` is what you publish.

**Payloads are bare where they can be.** A boolean goes out as `ON`/`OFF` and a number as digits, so a consumer needs no JSON parser; only structured data is JSON.

**Everything counts from 1**, because that is what is printed on the back of the box. A topic numbered 0 is rejected rather than treated as the first device.

onboard.description: The controller's mosquitto. iod (IO), ohc-audiod (audio) and sysmond (health) each publish their own topics on it; bridging to a house broker is mosquitto's bridge, set from the settings page.

browser.description: The same broker over WebSocket, proxied by webd on port 80 so a page needs one origin.

relayState.description: `ON` or `OFF`. n counts from 1, matching the terminal marking.

contactState.description: `ON` = CLOSED. Polled by iod; the driver caches it so many subscribers cost one UART round trip.

ledState.description: 0..max_brightness. Addressed by NAME — `power`, `wifi-red` — because LEDs are not a numbered row.

mcuLink.description: ANSWERING, not merely present. A wedged part leaves the gpiochip registered.

serialViewers.summary: How many clients hold this port open (retained)
serialViewers.description: One shared session per port: every viewer sees the same stream.

irRx.summary: A code the front receiver heard (NOT retained)
irRx.description: Pronto, in the same form `ir/front/send` accepts — so a learned code can be sent straight back.

serialRx.summary: Bytes arriving on a user port (NOT retained)

relaySet.description: `ON`, `OFF` or `TOGGLE`. Idempotent: the firmware has no SET opcode, so iod reads before it toggles.

ledSet.description: `ON`, `OFF`, or a number for brightness. A LED under a kernel trigger has the trigger dropped first — asking for a level is asking for software control.

irSend.description: port is a rear jack number, or `front` for the internal blaster — which is NOT jack 7; it has no socket. Type 0000 (learned) only, and a carrier word of 0000 is refused because the firmware divides by it.

serialWrite.summary: Write bytes to a user port

serialDtr.description: Only on ports whose connector carries the line (`modem: true` in the capability document): the DB9s on the HC-800 and IO Extender. Held ON from boot, as the stock `dtserver` does, because accessories such as a GC-IRL learner are powered from it.

serialSetDtr.description: `ON` or `OFF`. Refused on a port without the line. Dropping it power-cycles a line-powered accessory; the choice survives a baud change.

serialRts.description: Only on ports whose connector carries the line (`modem: true` in the capability document): the DB9s on the HC-800 and IO Extender. Held ON from boot, as the stock `dtserver` does, because accessories such as a GC-IRL learner are powered from it.

serialSetRts.description: `ON` or `OFF`. Refused on a port without the line. Dropping it power-cycles a line-powered accessory; the choice survives a baud change.

mcuReset.description: Recovery for a wedged part. Tries both polarities and reports which worked. Note: on the HC-800 a wedged MCU has NOT been recoverable by reset — it needs a power cycle.

audioOutputState.description: The device string the stock network receivers render to, e.g. `hw:DSP` (boards without named outputs). Absent/empty means they follow the system default PCM. Published by ohc-audiod; the list of outputs is its REST `/audio/api/audio`.

audioVolumeState.description: 0..100, read back from `amixer`. Best-effort: a card with no recognisable volume control simply never publishes this.

audioReceiverRunning.description: id is `librespot` (Spotify Connect) or `shairport` (AirPlay). These are receivers — playback is driven from the phone — so there is no transport here; this is only whether the daemon is running.

audioSetOutput.description: A device string from the `/api/audio` output list, e.g. `hw:DSP`. iod writes its selection file; the receivers apply it on their next restart.

audioSetVolume.description: A percent 0..100. Clamped, applied via `amixer`, and read back into the retained state topic.

raw.description: The escape hatch: the same enum the REST layer takes, e.g. `{"op":"relay.set","index":0,"on":true}`.

audioMap.description: Boards with named outputs: `outputs` and `inputs` (hardware), the configured `spotify`/`airplay` (name + output) and `routes` (input + output), and `instances` — every supervised process with its `running` flag and whether it is `playing`. JSON. Changing the map is configuration: REST `PUT /audio/api/audio/endpoints`.

healthNow.description: Every sampling period (5 s): `series` (sensor descriptions, once), `values` positional against it, `cpu`, `load1`, `mem_used_pct`, `uptime_s`, `mem_total_kb`. JSON.

healthHistory.summary: Telemetry history at one point a minute (retained, sysmond)
healthHistory.description: The sample ring downsampled to a point a minute (six hours ≈ 360 points); `period_s`, `series`, `samples`. Full-resolution windows are REST `/sys/api/history`.

healthFan.summary: Fan presence, mode and duty (retained, sysmond)
healthFan.description: `{available, mode: auto|manual, pct}`; `available:false` on boards with no controllable fan.

healthSetFan.summary: Hold the fan at a percent, or release it
healthSetFan.description: `auto` returns the fan to its temperature curve; a number 0..100 holds it there (a critical temperature still forces 100%). Boards with a fan helper only.

systemRestore.description: `{available, openhc, detail}` on boards with the ohc-restore helper (EA family, HC-800); `available:false` elsewhere.

systemRestoreStock.description: Acted on only for the literal payload `confirm`. One-way: the controller reboots into Control4's recovery and openHC is removed.

serviceStatus.description: `online` / `offline` (last will) for `audiod`, `sysmond`; iod's is `openhc/{box}/status`. Lets an integration tell which part of the box went away.

audioLevel.description: Boards with named outputs: the one volume of that jack. Every endpoint, route and announcement on the output goes through it, and its AirPlay/Spotify endpoints use it as their hardware mixer, so a phone volume slider moves it too; this topic shows whichever moved last. Audio taper (40·log10(100/p) dB); 0 mutes.

audioSetLevel.description: A percent 0..100 for output `{output}` (an id from state/audio/map). Saved across reboots.

audioAnnouncing.description: ON while an announcement plays on `{output}`; its music is ducked underneath.

audioAnnounce.description: Over `{output}` (or `all`): `chime` (or empty) for the built-in two-tone chime, an http(s) URL or an absolute path to a WAV. The output music ramps down (OHC_AUDIO_DUCK_DB, default 20 dB), the announcement plays at the output level, the music ramps back. One at a time per output; more queue.

audioMeta.summary: Now playing on an endpoint (retained, ohc-audiod)
audioMeta.description: Per Spotify/AirPlay endpoint (`tag` as in state/audio/map instances, e.g. `spotify-1`): `state` (playing/paused/stopped), `title`, `artist`, `album`, `cover` (an image URL, or for AirPlay a path under REST `/audio/api/audio/` such as `cover/airplay-1?v=3`), `client` (the phone or app), `duration_ms`. Cleared (empty retained message) when the session ends.

audioLibrary.description: Boards with a `library` endpoint: mpd playing the drives under /media. `state` (play/pause/stop/offline), `elapsed_s` with `elapsed_at_ms` (when it was read, so a client can run the clock), `duration_s`, `position`, `queue_length`, `random`, `repeat`, `updating` (indexing the drives). What it plays is `state/audio/meta/library-0`; its volume is its output level. Cleared when there is no library endpoint.

audioLibraryCommand.description: `play` [queue position], `pause`, `toggle`, `stop`, `next`, `previous`, `seek` <seconds>, `clear`, `add` <uri>, `replace` <uri> (clear, add, play), `random` ON/OFF, `repeat` ON/OFF, `update` (re-index). A uri is a path under /media as REST `GET /audio/api/audio/library/browse` returns it; a folder adds everything under it.

audioTone.description: Images with the tone stage (the ohceq ALSA plugin): `{knob}` is `bass` or `treble` (dB, -12..12; shelves at 120 Hz and 8 kHz) or `balance` (-100 left only .. 100 right only). Applies to everything on `{output}`. Boosting lowers the overall level by the boost, so nothing clips.

audioSetTone.description: `bass`/`treble` in dB (-12..12) or `balance` (-100..100), clamped. Heard at once (the plugin reads its controls as it plays) and saved across reboots.

audioInput.description: ON while `{input}` is playing to its default routes (the routes in state/audio/map). Every input starts OFF.

audioSetInput.description: `ON`, `OFF` or `TOGGLE`. An input route in the map is a default — where the input plays when triggered — so audio flows only while it is ON. Only that input’s routes start or stop; nothing else on the outputs is interrupted.

b64.description: base64, because a serial stream is not text
